title: The ideal: concert halls instead of smoky clubs
summary: Wilson says he wants to play four or five nights a week in concert halls, since jazz clubs are priced out and his last club sets drag.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Absolutely. Well, at this stage in your life, Teddy, if you had your druthers, what would you like to just do now? What would you like to play?

Well, I would just like to play in the concert field -- the two sets a night, about I'd say right now I'd like to play at least 4 or 5 nights a week, because while I don't want to be overworked, I must play -- if I don't play enough, I get rusty, and I have to keep the channels open.
The musical channels open. I've got to keep at it, you know, and just keep it open all the time.

You could absolutely do your best; you'd play for about an hour or you'd play 50 minutes and then take a little break, a 20 minute of 15 minute break, and then you could play another 50 minutes, and you could absolutely do your best.

But me, I find it's hard to really play well four times, 40 to 45 minutes a night. The last set is going to be dragging, you know, like the nightclub program. The best are those first ones. In a concert hall, it's perfect. With a fine
piano, the acoustics of a good room, and people who come there for nothing but the music -- they're not coming to buy a drink or to socialize with their friends; they're coming to hear music.

But of course, that's what jazz is -- and the jazz clubs are phased out -- economically, the high cost of musicians, and the public can't take the tariff to go to a jazz club and pay $5 or $6 for every set and get some bad whiskey; it's compulsory to drink bad whiskey and pay an admission, too, so that the concert field can't sustain everybody.

But I think I can get enough of that, mixed in with the four-a-night-in-the-room, in a 6-night-a-week or a 5-night-a-week job, to make it, keep it interesting. But if I had my druthers, as I said, it would be strictly that concert hall, Carnegie Hall, Symphony Hall, every night -- and no cellars, smoke-filled cellars with prostitutes sitting around, like the Europeans like to take their jazz in the cellar one flight below the street -- none of that!
For me, it's in a concert hall. But a 9-foot Steinway strictly.
Those ladies would probably love to hear you, Teddy!
Two sets, two sets, and then the encores.
